facts.raw_span: A 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor
a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extending craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle and smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, are consistent with a vestibular schwannoma.

The patient's imaging findings, including multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas and T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components, are consistent with a meningioma.

The patient's imaging findings, including curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci and smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, are consistent with a hemangioma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle and dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles, are consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas, are consistent with an epidermoid cyst.

The patient's symptoms, including bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor, and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle, are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma.

rationales.F05: Large mass at the cerebellopontine angle suggests a vestibular schwannoma or other tumor.
rationales.F06: Extension into the premedullary space is consistent with a tumor originating from the cerebellopontine angle.
rationales.F12: Smooth remodeling and erosion of bone is more typical of a chordoma or other slowly growing tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle and involvement of Meckel's cave, are more consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma, which is a type of tumor that arises from the trigeminal nerve.
